sections.html:
The state capital and seat of Anne Arundel County, Annapolis lies on the Chesapeake Bay where the Severn River meets it, about 25 miles south of Baltimore and 30 miles east of Washington, D.C. The 2020 census counted 16,751 households.

Inside city limits, the areas people name most are Church Circle and St. Anne's, Main Street and City Dock, State Circle and Maryland Avenue, West Annapolis, the West Street arts district, Eastport and Parole. Arnold, Crofton, Crownsville, Edgewater, Gambrills, Londontowne, Millersville and Odenton are county communities, so the city's tax and rules do not reach them. Annapolis is the only incorporated city in Anne Arundel County.

The Colonial Annapolis National Historic Landmark District surrounds City Dock. Ask the city planning office about review rules before you promise a buyer any exterior renovation near the historic area. Landmarks in the district include the Maryland State House, begun in 1772, the Old Treasury Building from 1735 and the Hammond-Harwood House from 1774, so older houses nearby may come with extra review and older systems that an inspector will flag. A seller with permits and repair records ready tends to keep a deal together when the inspection report arrives.

Water is the biggest risk for Annapolis owners. Sea level has risen about 15 inches over the past century, and Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed the storm surge to a record 7.58 feet.

  • Non-storm "sunny day" tidal flooding hit 18 days between May 2019 and April 2020, up from 12 days in 2018.
  • The 1995 to 2005 average was about 2 days a year.
  • The city recorded 120 flooding events in 2024.
  • Ground was broken on November 3, 2025 for an $87 million City Dock project with floodgates and raised land, designed to protect against flood levels through 2060.

A flood-damaged house can be hard to sell on the open market, because a buyer's inspector will note the damage. An as-is cash sale avoids the drying-out, repair and re-inspection cycle.

On September 1, 2021 an EF-2 tornado struck the western edge of the city with estimated winds of 125 mph. Tornado or hurricane surge damage can take insurers and contractors months to settle.

If you are selling a house with open storm damage, keep the claim file, the adjuster's report and any repair estimates together. A buyer paying cash will usually price the repairs into the offer, while a financed buyer may be held up by the lender's appraisal. Photos taken before and after cleanup, plus receipts for any emergency work, also help a buyer see what was fixed and what remains.

sections.h2: Property tax rates and due dates
sections.html:
One bill carries three rates, and payments go to Anne Arundel County. Below are the rates for the fiscal year of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

ChargeRate per $100 of assessed value
City of Annapolis$0.738
Anne Arundel County$0.577
State of Maryland$0.112
  • Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and the balance by December 31, with a 0.87% service charge on the second payment.
  • The Homestead Tax Credit caps yearly growth in taxable value for a primary home: 10% for the city and 2% for the county. Applications are due December 31 for a credit starting the next July 1.
  • The Homeowners' Property Tax Credit is income-based, and households under $60,000 should consider applying.
  • Finance Customer Service answers at 410-222-1144.

Each year the state reappraises a third of properties and spreads any increase over three years. Residential values in Anne Arundel County were 16.0% higher in the January 1, 2026 cycle than in 2023.

For Anne Arundel County the 2026 General Assembly staff table shows transfer tax of 1.0% to 1.5%, plus a 0.5% surcharge when a deal reaches $1 million. Recordation tax is $3.50 per $500, and the state adds its own 0.5% transfer tax.

The contract decides who pays each tax. A title company will print the numbers on the settlement statement, and you should ask for a draft early so no line surprises you at the table.

sections.h2: What an Annapolis seller must disclose
sections.html:
Anyone selling a one- to four-unit house must hand the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer form on or before signing the contract (Maryland Real Property Code 10-702). The disclaimer states that the property is sold as-is, except for latent defects the seller actually knows about.

Fiduciary sales in estates and trusts, bank sales after foreclosure and tax sales are exempt. A buyer who gets the form late can rescind within five days of receiving it.

Closing is where the tax and fee lines come together. The title company collects your payoff letter if there is a mortgage, pays any open property tax, and prints transfer and recordation tax on the settlement statement. Anne Arundel County receives the tax payments, even though the bill carries a city rate.

Because the bill is split into a city, county and state rate, ask the title company to show each piece if you are prorating the year with the buyer. If you have a homestead credit, the buyer will start fresh, and the buyer's first bill can be higher than yours was. That is worth a sentence in your conversation so nobody feels misled later. Written numbers on the settlement statement settle most arguments before they start. A seller with a flood-prone house should also be ready for the buyer's lender to ask about flood insurance before it will fund.

If you need to move quickly, tell the title company your target date at the first call. Payoff letters and tax certificates take time to arrive, and a short heads-up usually keeps a closing from slipping by a week.

sections.h2: Selling fast: what the steps look like
sections.html:
A fast sale here depends on a handful of steps, and most delay comes from paperwork rather than from the buyer.

  1. Pull the latest tax bill and note any unpaid balance, which the title company will pay from your proceeds.
  2. Fill in the disclosure or disclaimer form and have it ready for the contract.
  3. Collect flood, storm or insurance records for the house.
  4. Ask the title company for a draft settlement statement showing transfer and recordation tax.

A cash buyer typically skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, so closing can happen on a timeline you choose. That helps when the house has flood damage, deferred repairs or a tax balance you want cleared quickly.

faqs.q: What is the Annapolis property tax rate?
faqs.a: Three pieces apply for the year starting July 1, 2026: $0.738 per $100 for the city, $0.577 for the county and $0.112 for the state.

faqs.q: When are Annapolis property taxes due?
faqs.a: If it is your principal residence, half is due by September 30 and half by December 31, with a 0.87% service charge on the second half. For a full-year bill, call 410-222-1144 for the due date.

faqs.q: What is the Anne Arundel County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The 2026 staff table shows 1.0% to 1.5%, with a 0.5% surcharge at $1 million or more. A separate state transfer tax of 0.5% also applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Annapolis house with water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Disclose the damage and sell as-is. A cash buyer typically prices the repairs into the offer, which avoids a drying-out and re-inspection cycle.
